domain: Assay-office and hallmarking practice — cupellation and touchstone assay of precious metal, the Trial of the Pyx (independent jury judging sampled coin against a physical trial plate and a statutory 'remedy' tolerance, on its own balances), the sponsor/assay-office/standard/date mark chain as provenance, periodic verification of the trial plates themselves, and the assay register as the durable record
axioms: Independence lives in the sample, the standard, the method, and the instrument — not in the examiner; a second examination that shares all four with the first certifies nothing however skilled the second examiner is.

The standard is itself an artifact that can be wrong and must be periodically assayed; a trial run against an unverified plate inherits the plate's defect rate, and every verdict from it is uninterpretable.
The party that makes the piece cannot certify its own standard; the author of a criterion is not a neutral judge of whether the criterion measures the thing.
A verdict without a tolerance fixed in advance is not a verdict: the remedy band must be written before the piece is made, or PASS and FAIL absorb every ambiguous case at the examiner's discretion.
Weight and fineness are different properties: a measure certifies exactly one, and readers will assume it certifies the other unless the design pairs it with a second measure.

Universal examination is one option among several: sampling plus a durable register plus a credible counter-assay can carry the same assurance far more cheaply — but a mark is worth only what the counter-assay regime behind it is worth, and a stamp nobody ever re-tests degrades to decoration.
Without a register of verdicts and the criterion each turned on, a run of trials produces an impression, not evidence, and nothing can be calibrated afterwards.
primitives: assay method (the verify block as executed)
trial plate (the frozen criteria the verdict is measured against)
sample (the artifact and tree state actually examined)
second examination (the validator pass, and what it shares with the first)
remedy / tolerance band (the missing verdict between PASS and FAIL)
gauge defect (a criterion that measures the wrong thing — pilot-1's 6/6)
hallmark (the PASS verdict as a claim downstream parties act on)
counter-assay regime (what detects a false PASS, and who runs it)
sampling fraction (how much of production is examined at all)
weight vs. fineness (token-share gate vs. work correctness)
instrument independence (interstat profile.py relative to the party measured)
assay register (persisted per-item verdict, quoted criterion, executor report)
failure_mode: Indifferent to how the piece reached the examination: handoff losses, spawn-boundary state, stale preconditions, and half-applied trees are outside its frame entirely, so it will not notice a defect that never reaches a verdict.

Biased toward adding assurance machinery — registers, counter-assays, verified standards — and habitually under-prices the latency and cost of the regime it proposes; it has no way to feel that the ceremony might exceed the value of the goods being assayed.

Treats each item as a discrete piece with a stable identity, so it reasons poorly about work whose correctness is diffuse, aesthetic, or only visible across several items; anything without a stateable criterion looks to it like unassayable metal.
Cannot evaluate model capability, routing, or effort settings: 'who examines' is doctrinally irrelevant to it, so it will miss findings that turn on Sonnet's or Opus's specific competence.

Assumes an adversarial or careless producer whose incentive is to pass; where the producer is simply mistaken rather than motivated, some of its independence machinery is over-engineered and it will not say so.
Silent on organisational adoption — whether anyone will actually keep the register, run the counter-assay, or read the second measure — so it can specify a regime that is correct and unused.
